The neoplastic cells show strong and diffuse nuclear staining for ER. The palisading arrangement of the neoplastic cells is evident along and around the fibrovascular cores.

diagnosis: Solid papillary carcinoma in situ with invasion
legend: The invasive carcinoma is an invasive carcinoma of no special type (NST) comprising irregular neoplastic glands and trabeculae infiltrate the breast parenchyma adjacent to solid papillary carcinoma.

Invasive solid papillary carcinoma comprising confluent and anastomosing solid islands of tumour cells and few infiltrating strands with relatively bland, oval to round, vesicular nuclei without prominent nucleoli. Delicate and almost imperceptible vessels extend into the solid tumour nests. Some tumour islands have a jigsaw-like arrangement within desmoplastic stroma. A few puddles of extracellular mucin are present. In situ solid papillary carcinoma is also noted in this section, occurring within ducts as well as demonstrating circumscribed outlines.

Solid papillary carcinoma in situ shows expanded and dilated ducts that are partially filled by a solid monotonous epithelial cell population punctuated by fine congested vessels. Tumour cells show amphophilic cytoplasm. Perivascular pseudorosettes are present. Adjacent breast tissue shows atypical ductal hyperplasia.
